label: failover
type: removing an unavailable or failing node's active vBuckets from service by promoting replicas, in one of two kinds - graceful or hard. Distinct from node removal: a failed-over node's replica vBuckets are LOST at the next rebalance, where a removed node's are recreated elsewhere first.
evidence: There are two basic types: _graceful_ and _hard_.
Note that when a node is flagged for _failover_ (as opposed to _removal_), replica vBuckets are lost when rebalance occurs, following node-removal.
Both manual and automatic failovers can cause the loss of durably written data.
note: Parent of the graceful/hard pair and the term the whole manage-nodes/ subtree turns on. The failover-versus-removal contrast is the single most consequential sentence in round 26's scope and it is stated twice, on fail-nodes-over.md and remove-node-and-rebalance.md, from opposite sides - each page explains itself by reference to the other operation. Neither statement exists in learn/clusters-and-availability/.
relates_to_competency_question: What are the kinds of failover, and how does failing a node over differ from removing it?
